questions.q: Why do `unique` and `not_null` go on `fct_orders.order_id` specifically?
options: Because order_id is a string column, not a number
Because every column in every model needs both tests by default
Because dbt requires at least one test per model
fct_orders is one-row-per-order; not_null catches a dropped key, unique catches a join producing more than one row per order
questions.explain: These two tests directly match what could go wrong at this model's intended grain — one row per order.

questions.q: What does the `relationships` test on `fct_orders.customer_id` check?
options: That customer_id values are all unique
That every customer_id value in fct_orders actually exists in the customers mart
That customer_id is never null
That customer_id matches a specific regex pattern
questions.explain: relationships is a referential-integrity check: every value in this column must exist in the referenced model's column.

questions.q: Where does the list of valid values for the `status` accepted_values test come from?
options: Power BI's own default status categories
An arbitrary list invented for this lesson
The real status values recorded from `raw_orders` back in Lesson 1's lab
The Beginner project's customers mart
questions.explain: Lesson 1 had you query raw_orders directly and record the real status values present — that exact list is what accepted_values checks against.

questions.q: What does a failing `unique` test on `order_id` foreshadow in this chapter?
options: The exact failure Lesson 13 walks through diagnosing, caused by a join set up back in Lesson 6
That the whole dbt project needs to be rebuilt from scratch
A completely unrelated schema.yml syntax error
Nothing — it's just a routine test with no further relevance
questions.explain: This chapter deliberately returns to this exact test and failure mode in Lessons 13-15.

questions.q: What command runs the tests for all four new models at once?
options: `dbt run --full-refresh`
`dbt test --select fct_orders stg_jaffle_shop__orders stg_jaffle_shop__payments int_orders__joined`
`dbt docs generate`
`dbt compile --select tests`
questions.explain: dbt test --select, followed by the model names, runs just the tests attached to those models.
